plates.title: The Funnel, the Fork, and the Return
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page on cream vellum, drawn in iron-gall brown ink with gold leaf accents and touches of lapis and madder-red, in the hand of a single medieval illustrator, composition running top to bottom in a chain of round painted medallions linked by curling vine-tendrils that fork and rejoin like a genealogical tree. At the very top, a small brass automaton stands before a scribe's balance-scale weighing a heart against a sealed scroll. Below, a scribe's hand plaits three plain ribbons into a braid; beside it a folded, ribbon-like coiled shape sits ignored while robed figures admire a separate speaking mechanical mouth; beside that, tiny travelers climb a hillside path that turns vertical just ahead of their feet. These three tendrils braid together into a single medallion: a round bun marked with a faint accidental face, peered at by monks. From this medallion a tendril descends to four medallions in a row: a brain split into flesh and brass gears; an ornate bronze geared astronomical device with dials; a scholar gesturing to a glowing heart rooted in soil; a dry stomach-diagram beneath a rain-cloud whose drops stop short of it. These four tendrils converge into a leaning tower built of stacked cogs, visibly cracking. From the cracked tower, a tendril descends to a hooded figure at a misted crossroads holding a blank scroll toward failing light. From this figure the path forks into two medallions side by side: a forge where a craftsman hammers a small glowing homunculus while onlookers recoil holding out a chain; and a shelf of glass vessels each holding a tiny glowing knot of tissue, tended by an alchemist. Both forks rejoin at the bottom into a final medallion: a rough stone idol and a jointed brass figure standing side by side, leaning toward one shared small flame, with a slender gold tendril curling back up the right margin of the page to touch the scale-and-heart medallion at the top, closing the loop. Wide decorated margins, small painted foliage, no lettering, no numerals, no text anywhere on the page.

plates.title: Doing and Being, Bias and Rapture
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page on cream vellum, iron-gall brown ink with gold leaf and touches of lapis and madder-red, same single hand and palette throughout, composition in painted roundels linked by branching vine-tendrils, running top to bottom. At the top, a wide medallion shows a cluster of small figures at ordinary tasks: one bent over a grid of squares, one assembling wooden furniture, one walking a lane toward a shopfront carrying a basket. From this medallion two vine-tendrils branch left and right. The left branch descends through: a human figure standing at the centre of a compass-circle ringed by varied creatures and objects all facing inward; then a tall ladder rising through the page with winged angelic figures at its top rungs, human figures at its middle, and animals at its foot; then a crowd of robed figures gathered eagerly around a speaking mechanical mouth on a scroll-stand; then a sleeping figure in a curtained bed with a faint translucent figure standing at its foot. The right branch descends through: a road rising skyward that steepens sharply just ahead of a traveller's foot and flattens behind, the traveller gazing up in awe; then a robed inventor standing before a glowing jointed humanoid raised on a stone altar, arms lifted as if before a deity. Both branches, left ending at the bedside ghost and right ending at the altar scene, send their tendrils down to converge in a final medallion at the bottom of the page: a round bun bearing a faint accidental face, examined closely by two monks leaning in with lamps. Decorative foliate borders in the margins, small painted vines and leaves filling empty space, no lettering, no numerals, no text anywhere on the page.

plates.title: The Cornerstone and the Cracking Tower
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page on cream vellum, iron-gall brown ink with gold leaf and touches of lapis and madder-red, same hand and palette as companion pages, composition in painted roundels joined by branching vine-tendrils, running top to bottom. At the top, a single keystone crowning a stone archway bears upon it, side by side, a small brass gear and a softly glowing brain-shape. From this keystone, four vine-tendrils branch downward side by side into four medallions: a brain split down the centre into flesh on one side and brass gears on the other; an ornate bronze geared astronomical device with dials and toothed wheels; a robed scholar gesturing toward a glowing heart rooted among tangled soil; and a dry stomach-and-intestine diagram beneath a rain-cloud whose drops stop short of touching it. From the split-brain medallion, a further tendril descends to a row of three small heads shown in sequence, each more transformed than the last, flesh giving way piece by piece to brass cogs and plates. From the dry-stomach medallion, a tendril descends to a small stone office filled with dials and gearwork, its roof open to a storm-cloud from which hailstones fall inward onto the machinery. All four upper medallions, together with the transforming-heads sequence and the hail-filled office, send tendrils converging into one final medallion at the bottom: a tower built of stacked cogs and gears, leaning visibly, with cracks running down its stone base. Decorative foliate borders fill the margins with small painted vines and leaves, no lettering, no numerals, no text anywhere on the page.

vignettes.depicts: A single keystone at the top of a stone arch, with a small brass gear and a softly glowing brain-shape resting together upon it, both borne up by the one stone.
